headline: Quantum Computing Frontiers and Neural Network Verification
summary: Today's research spans fundamental quantum theory, quantum network synthesis, and hardware protection, alongside key algorithmic bounds for non-Markovian simulation and group designs. In classical verification, a new branch-and-bound framework tackles relational neural network robustness.

themes.title: Quantum Information & Circuit Theory
themes.body: Studies establish rigorous bounds in quantum theory, including the finite entanglement-breaking index of PPT channels, depth limits on group designs, and eavesdropping detection via indefinite causal order.

themes.title: Quantum Systems & Algorithms
themes.body: Advances across the quantum stack, presenting distributed Clifford circuit synthesis for network topologies, exponential speedups for non-Markovian simulation, and a protected Andreev spin qubit design.

themes.title: Neural Network Verification
themes.body: From followed authors, the SaBRe framework employs branch-and-bound relational neuron splitting to accelerate global robustness checks across large test suites.

connections.body: Both papers explore circuit complexity and expressivity limitations in structured quantum gate sets, focusing respectively on distributed Clifford synthesis and 1D depth lower bounds for Clifford and matchgate designs.
